title: Chapter 40: The Witchbeast’s Fangs
content:
Chapter 40:

The Witchbeast’s Fangs

His mind hurried, but his steps were cautious.

Subaru continued his trek through the dark night into the depths of the forest—following the words Lucas had desperately squeezed out from his hazy consciousness.

His mouth was dry, his throat burning with tension. Holding his breath, stifling his footsteps, he pushed on, ever onward through the forest of eternal darkness. While there was a faint trace of hesitation, there was no sign of the cowardice that would make him fear stepping forward.

Part of it was the big talk he’d given Rem, but Subaru didn’t think his actions were entirely without a chance of winning. To begin with, he didn’t rate himself highly enough to fearlessly dive into a situation with zero chance of victory.

Just as he had fallen completely from grace in his original world without any real reason, his self-evaluation in this world was rock bottom—with probably only total blockheads ranking below him.

Precisely because he made such judgments, he wouldn’t commit the folly of stepping into a completely unwinnable situation. Even in situations where he absolutely couldn’t back down, he had the pettiness and cowardice to look for excuses.

Because he was keenly aware of that, he could trace the thinnest of threads that others might overlook, struggling and clinging to an answer.

“Think back, review the situation. If this witchbeast really is just that little puppy…”

It was easy to fixate on the terrifying name and the actual lethal curse arts, but looking at it from a broader perspective, a path to victory began to emerge.

No matter how highly lethal the trap it set was, the entity behind it was still ultimately that frail little puppy. If his target was something that fit perfectly in a child’s hands, a creature whose combat power seemed equal to its adorable appearance, then,

“I shouldn’t lose to that… right?”

Banking on the opponent’s small size was a pathetic way to calculate his odds.

However, he didn’t think he was entirely off the mark. Subaru’s was a body already dispelled of the spell rite by Beatrice’s hand. That being so, if that creature tried to ensnare Subaru in its hex once again—it should be possible for him to drive home a decisive strike.

The hypothetical advantage in the event of a fight—that thin thread was the driving force supporting Subaru’s current steps. He was, of course, well aware that this was relying on the absolute most favorable conditions piling up for him.

Naturally, he could also imagine the exact opposite, the absolute worst-case scenario, but—

“No, no, stop it. If I picture the worst-case pattern, the god of this world loves to happily limbo right under that bar and hand me a situation even worse.”

Given his track record so far, he drew a defensive line before he could suffer any cruel retaliation. Even knowing that mercilessly ripping away that defensive line and gouging the wound hidden beneath was just this world’s way of showing affection.

“—!”

He caught his breath at a sudden sense of wrongness and stopped in his tracks.

The sensation of the air changing transmitted vividly to his skin, and he could feel the temperature of the clammy sweat of exhaustion running down his forehead rapidly plunging.

What pricked at his skin like needles was the aftershock of intimidation unconsciously released by an overwhelming presence. Just the fact that it was 

there

 was enough to make his instincts scream in terror.

As the ambient temperature shifted and the airflow twisted, it carried with it a foul stench. Into the forest, which until just a moment ago had been thick only with the smell of dense grass and soil, drifted a reek so raw and bloody it made him unconsciously grimace.

Unlike Rem’s extraordinary sense of smell, even Subaru’s completely ordinary nose could tell clearly. It was a raw stench unique to living creatures—or, more bluntly, the stench of a beast.

Unable to stop the mounting tide of a terrible premonition, Subaru held his breath and crept forward.

He quietly peeked through a gap in the trees, looking toward the source of the drifting stench—and realized that the thin thread he had been clinging to had been unceremoniously snapped.

—It was clad in pitch-black fur that blended perfectly with the deep darkness of the forest.

Its build was perhaps comparable to a large dog. Its long limbs planted firmly on the earth, supporting a heavy body that surely weighed no less than Subaru’s own.

The highly developed feral claws, and the fangs that couldn’t even be contained within its mouth, were the very crystallization of violence, evolved specifically to pierce and tear flesh.

In the darkness where the light was blocked by the canopy, only its glaringly bright red eyes were impossible to miss. They cast a dizzying, domineering gaze over the surroundings, looking as if they were waiting with bated breath for the moment to sink those fangs into its prey.

Just seeing that figure floating in the dark, it was blatantly clear.

—That grotesque form, pure threat extracted to its absolute limit, that was the witchbeast.

“And on top of that, it’s…”

Confirming its appearance in detail, Subaru touched his chin as he searched his memories.

The witchbeast visible right before his eyes—he recognized it.

It closely resembled the horned beast he had fought to the death at the end of the previous loop. At a glance, he couldn’t spot a horn on its forehead. But assuming it was the same one,

“Did I accidentally succeed in getting my revenge last time…?”

It wasn’t much of a consolation, but the thought that he had managed to strike back gave him a slight sense of vindication.

Of course, just as everything that happened in the previous loop remained only within Subaru, that fact couldn’t possibly bring about any change to the situation currently unfolding before him.

If there was any takeaway to be had,

“It’s just knowing that those claws and fangs aren’t just for show…”

He wasn’t exactly expecting a twist where the claws were fake and the fangs were just fashion, but simply knowing the threat was entirely real was enough to make his heart sink.

And with the confirmation of a large witchbeast’s presence, Subaru’s resolve also began to rapidly deflate. His already slim chances of winning had been completely wiped out.

Following his own self-assessment from earlier, his course of action should be to avoid anything reckless.

“Anyway, nice and slow…”

He was just deciding to back away from this place and wait to rendezvous with Rem when it happened.

“————”

Without taking his focus off the witchbeast, he stepped backward, keeping his glare fixed on its grotesque form. Then, in the corner of his slightly widened field of vision, something caught his attention.

In the abyss of the forest where the witchbeast stood, there was a place where fallen trees were piled on top of each other. Most likely, nestled in the gaps of those fallen trees was something akin to the witchbeast’s den.

—Beside those fallen trees, a single young girl had been tossed aside.

Torn, tattered clothes. Frayed brown braids. Blood seeped from her pale skin in various places, and from a distance, it was impossible to tell just how severely the body lying face-down was injured.

But, even so, that girl,

“—Urgh.”

A small, frail voice rang out.

Traveling through the air, piercing through the forest, it struck Subaru’s eardrums with undeniable force.

It was a distance it shouldn’t have been able to cross. Or perhaps it was just an auditory hallucination, an illusion that he had heard it.

Looking closely, the fallen girl wasn’t twitching a muscle, and for only her groaning breaths to reach him… as miracles go, it was an incredibly paltry wish to be granted.

The only one here was Subaru. Natsuki Subaru alone.

If a miracle was to occur, if the heavens truly wished to save the girl, then the one present should have been a much more dependable, strong, and heroic champion.

Someone like Roswaal. Someone like Beatrice. Someone like Reinhard.

If it were them, if it were her, they would have effortlessly blown past a situation like this. Trembling in fear with shaking knees, paralyzed like Subaru—it would be unthinkable for them.

They would easily swat away the threat of the witchbeast, rescue the girl from despair, and guide the story to a flawless happy ending. Amazing, cool, elegant.

But the one standing here was Natsuki Subaru.

He had no strength. No magic. No wisdom, nor the cleverness to be quick on his feet. If there was a miracle to cling to, he’d push through the crowds to snatch that right before anyone else. He was exactly that sort of unsalvageable man.

Desiring miracles—that was Subaru. Becoming a miracle himself was utterly impossible.

Subaru bit down hard on his back teeth, suppressing the urge for his teeth to start chattering.

He gasped, touching his chest as if to confirm the beating of his heart. It was beating. It was definitely beating, but he couldn’t tell if it was fast or slow.

The passage of time had become terribly ambiguous. His vision felt like it was warping and distorting; he wiped the sweat running down his forehead, rubbed his eyelids, and tried to stick to his original plan—to thoroughly play the bystander.

And yet,

“Hey, stop it…”

A weak mutter. Following his gaze, the witchbeast slowly swiveled its neck, looking toward the fallen girl. Then, scraping the ground with its sharp claws, it moved toward her with a leisurely gait. Step by step, step by step, as if scraping away at Subaru’s very soul.

He couldn’t read the witchbeast’s intentions. It must have been the one who dragged her all the way here. It could have killed her at any given moment. Yet it had kept her alive. Now, because the girl it kept alive had moved, it was trying to put a stop to it. It made no sense. It was unreasonable. It would reach her in just a few more steps. Wait, this was wrong, it made no sense. Just what should he do? Any chance of winning, any odds of victory, nowhere to be seen. The thread to cling to, no longer there, nothing, just,

—If it were Emilia, she surely wouldn’t hesitate.

“…Hey hey, hey hey 

hey hey hey hey

, I’m thinking something real stupid right now.”

He took a deep breath, steadied his breathing, dug his nails into his shaking knees, and bit his lip. He bit down hard enough to draw blood, using the pain to snap his consciousness fully awake.

Natsuki Subaru couldn’t perform miracles. All he could do was be endlessly ungraceful—struggling, thrashing, and throwing a tantrum at the encroaching despair, screaming that he didn’t want it, just to make things difficult. That was the extent of his abilities.

Subaru didn’t overestimate himself. Therefore, he could clearly see the limits of what he could do.

Leaving a tiny, insignificant scratch on destiny was his limit. And if he could see that limit, that absolute best he could do—then that much, at least, he had to accomplish.

He stripped off his jacket, wrapping the frayed butler outfit tightly around his left arm. He bound it firmly so it wouldn’t come loose, wiped the blood from his mouth, faced forward, and,

“ORAAAAAA!!”

Raising a furious roar, he kicked aside the vegetation and lunged into the space where the witchbeast readied itself.

Startled by the sudden shout, the witchbeast violently shuddered and leaped back, lowering its stance and glaring at Subaru.

Subaru, too, rallied himself with his screams, stomping the ground in a display of intimidation.

“Aaah! Over here! Hey, look at me! What’s wrong, you scared?!”

He bellowed, spit flying from his mouth. His heart was pumping an explosive, agonizing pain through his entire body.

Standing face-to-face like this, the witchbeast’s frame felt far larger than he had imagined. Part of that was due to observing it from a distance earlier, but a huge factor was being overwhelmed by its crushing hostility.

What he had learned from his fight with the witchbeast in the previous loop was that, despite the grandiose title of ‘witchbeast,’ the way it fought didn’t stray outside the bounds of the beasts Subaru was familiar with.

Granted, it wasn’t as if Subaru had ever had the opportunity to cross blows with a four-legged beast in his original world, but he had seen humans fight beasts countless times in manga and anime.

And among those, the most effective strategy against an opponent that relied on biting as its main weapon was exactly what Subaru was doing now—covering his arm in thick fabric.

Factoring in his meager equipment, it was the only countermeasure Subaru could muster.

Screaming, yelling, and intimidating, he thrust his left arm out in front to keep it in check.

The best outcome would be if the witchbeast turned out to be cowardly and fled, overwhelmed by Subaru’s fighting spirit. But just like last time, these creatures never let a target escape once they’d marked it as prey.

In stark contrast to Subaru’s roars shattering the forest’s silence, the low-crouching witchbeast didn’t let out a single growl. It merely coiled its four limbs in complete silence, glaring at Subaru as if calculating the precise moment to detonate its energy.

Its very demeanor seemed to clearly state which of them was the prey, causing Subaru’s voltage to spike even higher. Riding that momentum, he took another step forward,

“What’re you acting so cocky for?! Come on!! Bring it! Br—”

It vanished.

Just like that, the witchbeast that should have been right in front of him melted into the darkness and disappeared.

His throat froze in shock, and feeling the twitching tremble of his eyelids, Subaru realized his blunder—it had stolen the exact moment he blinked. The witchbeast had been waiting for the exact timing, even a split second, when Subaru would lose sight of it.

He shuddered at the fact that a wild beast could execute such advanced tactics—waiting for an opening in an opponent it was facing down. He immediately sent his gaze darting around, searching for the vanished witchbeast’s whereabouts,

—The instant the scene flashed across his mind, Subaru leapt in place, jerking his right leg back.

“————!”

“Serves you right! How do you like that!!”

With a high-pitched snap, the witchbeast’s fangs clamped down on the empty space where his right leg had just been. Having evaded an attack that would have gouged his nerves had he been a fraction of a second slower, Subaru brought a vicious stomp straight down onto the witchbeast’s wide-open torso.

A downward kick launched from an unbalanced posture was far from his full strength. However, it still dealt damage to the witchbeast, sending it tumbling as it let out a yelp that sounded exactly like a puppy’s.

Perhaps feeling humiliated by its own feeble cry, the witchbeast regained its footing, glared at Subaru, and finally bared its fangs, letting out a ferocious roar.

Its red eyes were dyed in furious rage, its fangs clashing together repeatedly within its drooling maw.

—That previous strike was pure luck. In the last loop, it had chosen to attack his leg first, so he merely trusted it would do the same and hit the jackpot.

“Hey, come on, come on! I’m sure you’re pretty pissed right now, but I’m way more pissed off than you are, you bastard!!”

—

Here it comes!

A conviction devoid of any evidence, but simultaneously, the witchbeast disappeared.

By the time it reappeared, it was already right in front of him, having circled to his left, sinking its long fangs into the arm he had thrust forward.

The sensation of sharp fangs tearing through thick fabric and burying themselves deep into the flesh beneath.

“I—!!”

An agonizing pain that almost made him burst into tears, a sharp agony that directly assaulted his cranial nerves.

But,

“—t doesn’t hurt!!”

He poured strength into his left arm, flexing the muscles. Naturally, this made it harder for the embedded fangs to pull out, and combined with the tangled jacket, it completely halted the witchbeast’s movements.

Its red eyes and Subaru’s gaze locked, and as he felt himself almost being swallowed by its overwhelming malice,

“You bit me, you absolute moron!!”

Hooking his left arm entirely around the witchbeast’s body, Subaru spun with all his might. Centrifugal force lifted the creature’s frame, and carrying the momentum of the spin, he slammed its back against a massive tree behind him.

He thought he heard a pained yelp, but Subaru didn’t stop there. Refusing to let go of the situation where he had its deadly fangs pinned, he swung his body wildly over and over, frantically smashing the prey in his arm against trees, against the ground, thrashing and battering it repeatedly.

And finally,

“It’s over!!”

Swinging it straight down onto a fallen log, he moved to crush the witchbeast’s face.

A brutal impact reverberated back into his arm, and the witchbeast’s body, which had been struggling to break free until a moment ago, suddenly went limp.

Panting heavily at the anticlimactic response, Subaru collapsed to his knees right there.

Looking closely, there was no life left in the eyes of the witchbeast still clamped onto his left arm. Profuse amounts of blood spilled from its violently crushed head, and a tree branch that had impaled it during one of the many slams jutted out from its back.

Slowly, he pried its jaws open and removed the fangs. Its tongue lolled out limply. Seeing that its life functions had completely ceased, Subaru took a massive gasp, finally breathing again.

“Did I… win?”

Muttering only that in a daze, he removed the blood- and saliva-soaked jacket from his left arm. The skin beneath the jacket was in terrible shape; the piercing fangs had gouged the flesh, and the white bone underneath was faintly visible.

The pain he had forgotten in his adrenaline-fueled state came rushing back upon staring directly at the wound. Grimacing heavily at the burn-like agony,

“Anyway… ah, it hurts. Shit, what about the kid…”

Crawling at an agonizingly slow pace, he somehow made it further in, reaching the girl beside the fallen tree.

Even though it was a battle with his life on the line, he felt not a single shred of accomplishment or realization of victory. All he had was a sudden, crushing fatigue that made his body heavy, and a strong sense of revulsion that made him want to wipe the exchange of murderous intent that had just occurred entirely from his mind.

He didn’t need elation or the afterglow of victory right now. Rather, the impatient desire to confirm whether he had recovered what he sought at the end of that struggle won out by far.

“—I’m just glad it wasn’t all for nothing.”

Cradling his left arm, Subaru slumped his back against the fallen tree and let out a deep sigh of relief.

That was because he could confirm that the breath of life still remained in the body of the girl right beside him—faintly dirtied with soil and blood. In fact, her complexion was much healthier compared to the children from earlier, and aside from minor external scratches, the damage was extremely light. Subaru, whose bone was showing in his left arm, was in much more critical condition.

“Making us worry like that… well, whatever. If a girl was left with scars on her body, I’d have to take responsibility and make her my bride, after all. And Emilia-tan seems like she’d be pretty strict about polygamy.”

Once a flood of relief washed over him, what returned to stabilize his mind was his usual flippancy.

He had told Rem he’d buy time, but as it turned out, he had spectacularly eliminated the threat itself. It surely wouldn’t hurt to be a little proud of himself.

“Something along the lines of, ‘Buying time is fine, but you don’t mind if I just go ahead and defeat it, right?’”

A pretty great outcome—he had managed to fulfill the long-cherished ambition that went unfulfilled in the source material.

To distract himself from the pain of his wound, his rambling thoughts continued in loops. He wanted to somehow carry the girl to the village, but in his current state, he didn’t have the stamina left to do so.

The best move would be to wait quietly for Rem to join them. This time, there was no time limit. Worst case scenario, even if he fell asleep right here, things would work out somehow.

“Though it’s not like I can just openly snooze right now…”

He retied the unwound jacket, having it serve as a tourniquet, and took a breath.

Then, Subaru’s ears suddenly picked up the distant sound of bushes rustling.

He raised his head. Just as he wondered if he had mistaken the sound of the wind, he heard the same noise again coming straight from the front—from the direction Subaru had lunged out of.

The direction Subaru had lunged from also happened to be the direction where he had parted ways with Rem. If so, then the one rustling the bushes must be that dashing blue-haired girl.

“I’m tired of waiting… Unfortunately, there are no opponents left for you.”

Preparing a line like that, which he’d always wanted to say at least once, he waited for the girl he was meeting up with to come bursting through.

The vegetation swayed, and there was a presence stopping just beyond the thicket. Feeling a gaze observing him, Subaru gave a wry smile.

He raised his right hand, intending to tell her that there were no longer any enemies to be wary of,

—When his whole body captured a suffocatingly thick wave of feral stench drifting over once again.

The bushes rustled, and a short, four-legged shadow stepped out from the other side.

And then,

“Hey, hey, you’ve gotta be kidding me…”

Red eyes brilliantly slicing through the night forest—he saw countless points of that light peering from beyond the cluster of trees in front of him.

So many it made him sick to even try counting, there were likely more than all the fingers and toes on his body combined.

Still clutching his left arm, he stood up, looked over the points of light floating in the darkness, and exhaled deeply.

Suddenly, Subaru touched his cheek with his right hand and realized his face was contorted. The corners of his mouth were twitching, forming the shape of a smile.

Ah, I see. Yeah, definitely, this would make you laugh in spite of yourself.

“—I’m dead, aren’t I.”

Overwhelming murderous intent exploded at that single utterance, and the silent forest was swallowed in a frenzy.

The only thing Subaru could do was shield the still-unconscious girl behind him, spread his arms wide to stand in their way, and show his own stubborn pride.

—Screaming trailed high, high up into the forest sky.
